correctness.rationale: For e_i e_j=e_{2j-i mod4}, the two-dimensional right annihilator R=span(e0-e2,e1-e3) is intrinsic. If char!=2, U=span(e0+e2,e1+e3), action on R has distinct ± parity characters and forces the shear to zero, quotient identity or swap, and diagonal/antidiagonal invertible R action. In char2, basis (e0,e1,u=e0+e2,w=e1+e3) yields product (x+ρ)(y+σ)=ε(y)(x+ρ)+(x0 y1)u+(x1 y0)w; quotient columns of idempotents force P∈{I,S}, restriction on R equals P and arbitrary shear T∈M2(k). Their composition is M2(k)^+ ⋊ C2 with swap conjugation. Orders 2(q-1)^2 or 2q^4 follow. Independently checked all 32 predicted GF2 block maps against every 16 basis product pairs; the unrestricted theorem rests on the algebraic block reduction.
